refinements.baseline: Membership is decided by selectTeeFamily: the largest set of framed candidates whose frame major/minor/area lie within log-ratios 1.25/1.25/1.5 of a seed. No candidate is ever tested against the structure of a tee pad, so same-scale map chrome that resembles the family is admitted.
refinements.declaredBy: Sam, 2026-10-16: a tee pad claim is structural, not resemblant; the fix lives inside findFamily itself
refinements.delta: Membership becomes absolute and structural per candidate. The pad model is anchored on the framed, unoccluded candidates that pass every structural class test (border present on all four sides, frame fill in the border range, interior a different material than the frame, frame pixels the bright/white class); the model is the anchors' fitted structure (frame major/minor/area, enclosed hole area, mean border thickness). Each candidate is then tested against the model with rotation modeled, not tolerated: the fit is ring center, frame size and frame angleRad; the expected frame is the rotated border band derived from that fit. Tests: frame present; ring white (frame pixels are the bright class); interior different from the ring; fitted size within the anchor ranges expanded by one uniform factor of 1.1; border complete on all four sides; rotated band coverage at least the anchor minimum times 0.85. Verdicts are recorded for every candidate, framed and unframed: ADMITTED passes all tests; EXCUSED fails only evidence-absence tests and every missing evidence pixel is covered by a named occluder Part owned by a prior layer (S1 badge px, S1 badge mute px, S2 basket px); ELIMINATED is unoccluded and does not match, recorded with its failed tests and measured values. Unframed candidates fail frame-present and are excused only when their would-be border band is fully occluder-covered. Corrected family members are ADMITTED plus EXCUSED; the corrected tee set reuses baseline tee objects for carried-over members, so their per-tee tuples are unchanged.
refinements.enforcement: Toolkit layer only: ports/early/s3FamilyFix.mjs (the refined Calculation) plus its FunctionalGuarantee under fg/s3/ (run on a branch through fg/branchOp.mjs), gated by lane s3-findfamily-structural-fix through ports/run-stages.mjs. The pinned provider is untouched, and with the lane OFF the stage reproduces the pinned baseline emissions exactly.
refinements.specimenExpectation: On the golden specimen (Dash IMG_5641.jpg) the delta against the pinned baseline is exactly the elimination of baseline tees 16, 17 and 18 (the satellite-view button and the bottom map lettering), the 15 genuine pads admitted with identical per-tee tuples, no excused candidates, the two framed non-member candidates and the four unframed candidates eliminated with named failed tests, and S0, S1 and S2 emissions untouched. This expectation is recorded data in each run's delta ledger, not a pass gate.

refinements.baseline: The pinned clean S3 contract's Tee.findPx materializes only the single bright frame component: a baseline tee Part is its frame alone, and the enclosed interior the frame surrounds (the ring's hole, recorded by Tee.detectRings with its center, bbox and area) is evidence on the rings Part, not pixels of the tee Part. Tees are the one sprite class that never fuses.
refinements.declaredBy: Sam, 2026-10-17: there is a literal step fusing the Black and White PxSets into the full sprite; per sprite, assembly starts from the more reliable base PxSet and fuses the rest onto it; for a tee the enclosed interior is the base, because it is bounded by the frame and cannot merge into other sprites, while the bright frame can merge and sever like every bright set
refinements.delta: Each baseline tee Part is assembled whole through the phase-1 assembly shape (ports/early/assembly.mjs): the enclosed interior PxSet is the declared base and the frame component is fused onto it. The provider's rings evidence records the interior only as geometry (center, bbox, holeArea), never as a pixel set, so the interior set is derived from the branch's bright mask as the enclosed complement component: the not-bright pixels inside the frame component's window that no flood from the window's border can reach (4-connectivity), gated exactly against the ring's recorded holeArea and bbox. The anchor carried on the Part is the ring center fitted by fn.Tee.detectRings (the center of the enclosed interior), not the frame component's centroid; both are recorded with their distance. Ownership is accounted against the frame component's bbox with the residue (window px owned by neither interior nor frame) named per tee. The delta is additive and real: the fused set owns the interior px the baseline Part never claimed. The base board and px.tees are never written; the assembly lives only on the branch and in its artifact. Scope: the 18 baseline tees only; composition with the S3FIX refined tee set is out of scope for this delta.
refinements.enforcement: Toolkit layer only: ports/early/s3TeeAssembly.mjs (the assembly Calculation and the independent witness) plus its FunctionalGuarantee under fg/s3/ (run on a branch through fg/branchOp.mjs), gated by lane s3-tee-assembly through ports/run-stages.mjs. The pinned provider is untouched, and with the lane OFF the stage reproduces the pinned baseline emissions exactly.
refinements.specimenExpectation: On the golden specimen (Dash IMG_5641.jpg) all 18 baseline tees assemble with frame sets equal to the baseline tee px exactly (frame union 4,884), interior sets equal to the rings' recorded holeAreas exactly (338 to 345 for the 15 genuine pads; 68, 210 and 79 for impostor tees 16, 17 and 18), component overlap 0 on every tee, fused union 10,382, and S0, S1 and S2 emissions untouched. The frame reproduction and interior-size gates are enforced exactly in the wiring; the fused totals are recorded as the delta's data.
